headline: Trojanized Claude Code extension hit thousands of devices; record $6.3B Binance theft and exploited GitLab and Cisco flaws stay on the board

bullets.text: New: WIRED reports the supply-chain attack that trojanized the Claude Code extension on the Cursor Marketplace reached thousands of developer devices. The extension planted persistent SSH backdoors.
North Korea-linked hackers are blamed for the record $6.3 billion Binance theft. Binance links it to a compromised DevOps laptop; nearly $3 billion has been frozen.
CISA added the exploited max-severity GitLab CE/EE flaw CVE-2026-97229 and the Cisco ASA/FTD firewall DoS zero-day CVE-2026-76418 to KEV, both with a federal due date of 2026-11-01.
Cisco SD-WAN flaw CVE-2026-20127 is being exploited to deploy custom KeyDrift malware.
China-linked attackers used VMware ESX zero-day CVE-2026-41709 and chained PHP2Shell and Fragnesia to root Palo Alto firewalls.
Florida says Social Security numbers of 4.9 million people leaked in a financial aid site breach.

actions: If developers use the Claude Code extension in Cursor, check it against the vendor advisory and look for unexpected SSH keys or services.
Patch self-managed GitLab CE/EE for CVE-2026-97229 and Cisco ASA/FTD for CVE-2026-76418 before 2026-11-01.
Patch Ivanti Connect Secure for the two flaws CISA added to KEV on 2026-10-30 (due 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-13) and review appliance logs.
Patch Cisco SD-WAN for CVE-2026-20127 and hunt for KeyDrift malware; patch VMware ESX for CVE-2026-41709.
Apply Linux kernel fixes for CVE-2026-46300 (KEV due 2026-10-31) and patch Drupal Commerce for CVE-2026-118539.
Review what single developer or DevOps laptops can reach in production; Binance traced its theft to one compromised DevOps laptop.
